title: Formal common-refinement and staircase coherence for compactifications
statement:
Let $\mathscr S$ be a category of schemes and separated finite-type morphisms, containing the compactifications and fibre products mentioned below. A compactification of $f:X\to Y$ is a factorization $X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY$ with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper; a refinement $c'\to c$ is a proper map of ambient schemes over $Y$ restricting to the identity on $X$. Suppose these categories are nonempty and cofiltered (common refinements exist and parallel arrows can be equalized), and compatible compactification towers and common refining towers exist as in [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower, lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered]. Suppose the same compatible staircases can be chosen for three composable morphisms.

Assign to each scheme $X$ a category $\mathcal D_X$. To each proper map $p:X\to Y$ assign $P_p:\mathcal D_X\to\mathcal D_Y$, and to each open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ assign $J_j:\mathcal D_U\to\mathcal D_X$, with unital associative natural composition isomorphisms $P_qP_p\simeq P_{qp}$ and $J_kJ_j\simeq J_{kj}$. For every proper/open square $pk=ir$, specify a natural isomorphism $\gamma_Q:J_iP_r\simeq P_pJ_k$, satisfying identity, horizontal and vertical pasting with those compositors, as in the formulas of [lem-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-pasting]. Put $H_c=P_pJ_j$. For a refinement $v:c'\to c$, define $\rho_v:H_c\to H_{c'}$ by $P_p$ applied to $\gamma$ for the square $vj'=j\operatorname{id}_X$, followed by the proper compositor.

The $\rho_v$ satisfy identities and composition, and $\rho_{v_1}^{-1}\circ\rho_{v_2}:H_{c_2}\to H_{c_1}$ for a common refinement $c'\xrightarrow{v_i}c_i$ is independent of that common refinement and its arrows and satisfies the cocycle law. For a compatible tower for $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, write $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$, $q:\overline Y\to Z$, $a:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$, $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$, $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $r:V\to Y$, and $j:X\hookrightarrow V$ with $bj=a$. The transformation
$$P_qJ_iP_rJ_j\xrightarrow{P_q\gamma_QJ_j}P_qP_pJ_bJ_j\simeq P_{qp}J_a$$
commutes with common-refinement comparisons between any two such towers. For a three-map staircase the two iterated transformations agree under the $\rho$ comparisons and compositors; identity towers give identity transformations. This is a formal assertion about the supplied $P,J,\gamma$ data; it assumes, and does not prove, the geometric existence or invertibility hypotheses.

proof.text: Insert the identity isomorphism in rho, specialize verticalIdentity and pLeft, and cancel the inverse proper unit. For composition, apply vertical pasting to the two refinement squares; naturality moves the inserted proper identity across gamma, pLeft cancels it, and pAssoc combines the outer proper compositors. These are the proved refinementOpenIso_comp and rho_comp calculations.

For parallel arrows, use Geometry.equalize to find a common precomposition on which they agree. The composition law and cancellation of its rho show their rho maps agree. For two common refinements use Geometry.common, compute comparisons on that refinement and use parallel independence. Compute all three terms of the cocycle on one common refinement and cancel the middle inverse.

Apply the local single-tower refinement equation to both arrows from the supplied common refining tower. Cancel the output refinement isomorphism and use horizontal-composition exchange to cancel the two input inverses. This proves the comparison equation for arbitrary supplied towers.
Apply the supplied-staircase calculation to the given Tower.

For the left identity tower use jLeft and pLeft, naturality of pId, and verticalIdentity. For the right identity tower use jRight and pRight and horizontalIdentity. Extensionality of natural transformations identifies the components.
